sources.title: Where this comes from
sources.disclaimer: Selfinder is a self-reflection practice, not medical advice, diagnosis, or treatment. The ideas here — including the map of seventeen states and the psychological concepts referenced on each level's page — are drawn from the named sources below. If you're struggling with your mental health, please talk to a doctor or a licensed mental health professional.
sources.influencesIntro: These aren't cited for any specific claim in the app the way the sources above are — they're the broader reading and thinking that shaped Selfinder's own tone and stance while it was being built. The five philosophers you walk with in the app (Socrates, Marcus Aurelius, Kierkegaard, Camus, Aristotle) belong here too, in spirit — they're not repeated below since they already have their own presence throughout the app.

howToUse.title: How to use Selfinder
howToUse.intro: A few ways of touching the app that aren't always obvious at a glance.
howToUse.saveBody: Wherever you see a glowing image or figure — the aura on Depths, a Card, Feeling Lucky's message, the kaleidoscope on Your Arc — press and hold to save it to your own photo gallery.
howToUse.ringBody: On the Levels map, and wherever a reading's own wheel appears, drag your finger around the ring to feel your way through the states — it names whatever you're pointing at and settles on release.
howToUse.guideHeading: Talk with your philosopher from Depths
howToUse.guideBody: Guide no longer has its own tab — tap your philosopher's name near the top of Depths any time to open a conversation, reading or no reading required.
howToUse.profileBody: Language, theme, reminders, and your account now live behind the small figure icon in the top corner of Depths, Journeys, and Your Arc.

guide.chooseSomeone: Choose who walks beside you in the You tab to begin.
guide.measureExplainer: A short conversation about your body, mind, heart, and spirit. At the end, {{name}} reflects the state emerging from your answers.

products.title: Journeys
products.tabExplainer: Something you wish you understood — and want an answer to now.
products.intro: A generated experience, made fresh each time you open it — separate from Your Arc's ongoing record.
products.centerDescription: A kaleidoscope and light cone made from your saved history — a new result every time you get it.
products.controlDescription: What am I really trying to control?
products.controlGrounding: Grounded in psychoanalytic thought on control, mastery, and anxiety — Freud, Klein, Winnicott.
products.theChoiceGrounding: Grounded in Self-Determination Theory and Winnicott's true self / false self.
products.theLoopDescription: Why does this keep happening to me?
products.theLoopGrounding: Grounded in Freud's repetition compulsion, transference, and Bowlby's internal working models.
products.whoseVoiceDescription: Is this really what I believe or want?
products.whoseVoiceGrounding: Grounded in Freud's superego, Horney's "tyranny of the shoulds," and Self-Determination Theory.
products.theRoadNotTakenDescription: Why can't I stop thinking about what could have been?
products.theRoadNotTakenGrounding: Grounded in research on counterfactual thinking and regret.
products.lettingGoDescription: What am I actually holding onto?
products.lettingGoGrounding: Grounded in contemporary grief research and the continuing bonds framework.
products.theMirrorDescription: Why does this person affect me so strongly?
products.theMirrorGrounding: Grounded in transference research and the Core Conflictual Relationship Theme.
products.theUnsaidDescription: What do I actually want to say?
products.theUnsaidGrounding: Grounded in Freud's work on inhibition and psychodynamic thought on expression.
products.becomingGrounding: Grounded in Erikson's identity development and Markus & Nurius's possible selves.
products.theThresholdDescription: What is stopping me from moving forward?
products.theThresholdGrounding: Grounded in approach-avoidance conflict and loss aversion research.
products.possibleSelvesDescription: Which future actually feels like mine?
products.possibleSelvesGrounding: Grounded in Markus & Nurius's possible selves and self-concordance research.
products.enoughDescription: What would actually be enough for me?
products.enoughGrounding: Grounded in research on the hedonic treadmill and maximizing vs. satisficing.

measureIntro.title:
A conversation to read
where you are right now
measureIntro.copy: {{name}} will ask you about four sides of your life — body, mind, heart, and spirit. Share what is actually true, not what you think it should be. The reading emerges from what you say.

spill.title: Write without looking back
spill.copy1: For one minute, just keep writing. Whatever comes, in any order, without editing it — you'll only ever see the word you're writing right now, nothing before it. When the minute is up, you can read the whole thing back.
spill.copy2: There's no wrong way to do this. Typos, half-thoughts, and repeats are part of it.

spillReveal.kept: Kept — you can find it later from your account.
spillReveal.keepNeedsConsent: Turn on saving your data in account settings to keep entries like this

levels.title: The map of consciousness
levels.copy: Seventeen states, none of them better or worse than another — drag around the wheel to see where each one sits.
levels.note: These connections describe what's true between neighboring states, not a route everyone has to walk — you can move from Anger to Love and back to Reason without passing through everything between, and that's not doing it wrong.

crisisSupport.title: If it's more than a wish
crisisSupport.body: What you wrote sounds like it might be more than Selfinder can hold. There are people trained for this, ready right now — reaching out isn't a step down from anything.
crisisSupport.call988Sublabel: Suicide & Crisis Lifeline — free, 24/7, in the US
crisisSupport.findHelplineSublabel: findahelpline.com — a directory of local crisis lines
crisisSupport.footnote: You can come back to Selfinder whenever you're ready. Nothing here was saved.
